claim: Section 3.6 stochastic ordering result (likelihood ratio order)
quote: Let X1 ~ MOEGE(alpha_1, eta, rho) and X2 ~ MOEGE(alpha_2, eta, rho). The random variable X1 is stochastically [smaller] than X2 in the: Stochastic order (X1 <=st X2) if the corresponding CDFs satisfies F_{X1}(x) <= F_{X2}(x) for all values x; Hazard rate order (X1 <=hr X2) if the corresponding CDFs satisfies h_{X1}(x) <= h_{X2}(x) for all values x; Likelihood ratio order (X1 <=lr X2) if f_{X1}/f_{X2} is a decreasing function. ... d/dx log[f_{X1}/f_{X2}] = ... < 0. If alpha_1 < alpha_2 for all values of x greater than zero. Then it follows from the implications of stochastic ordering that: X1 <=lr X2 => X1 <=hr X2 => X1 <=st X2.
family: Marshall-Olkin Extended Generalized Exponential MOEGE(alpha, eta, rho), common eta and rho
compared: tilt parameter alpha_1 vs alpha_2 (alpha_1 < alpha_2)
